newsitem.title: USA: Holder asks Shoney's to rescind amendements.
newsitem.headline: Holder asks Shoney's to rescind amendements.

text.p: A dissident shareholder said Thursday he urged Shoney's Inc to rescind its recently amended bylaws and agree to an August 19 special meeting date.

In a June 25 letter to Shoney's, Raymond Schoenbaum wrote "your stated purpose in adopting the Bylaw amendments were to clarify the special meeting process. ... If you are sincere in this regard, we request that you rescind these amendments."
The restaurant chain amended its bylaws on June 24, but Shoenbaum, son of the man who founded Shoney's, contended that it was done to entrench the company's management.

In the letter, disclosed in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Schoenbaum writes "we will not allow the board and the management of the company to apply these amendments to the actions taken by us over the last week."
"If necessary, we are prepared to go to court to enforce our legitimate rights," Schoenbaum said.
"To require us to engage in a court battle with the current Board and management to enforce our legitimate rights would not be in anyone's interest," he wrote.
Schoenbaum requested Shoney's board respond to his letter by the close of business on June 26. Schoenbaum and his mother formed the Shoney's Shareholder Committee with their eight percent stake.
